speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
text: asked the Minister for Manpower with regard to the recent cases of Android users losing close to $100,000 of CPF savings through malware-related scams (a) how many similar malware-related scams has the Ministry detected in the past three years; (b) what are the safeguards that the Ministry intends to implement to prevent CPF savings being lost to scammers; and (c) what recourse will the victims have with regard to their lost CPF savings.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: So, even though nine involved unauthorised CPF withdrawals, the ninth case itself did not result in the loss of CPF savings because the Singapore Police Force (SPF) managed to stop the transfer out from the bank account of the CPF member.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: CPF monies were paid from members' CPF accounts to their own bank accounts and then they were subsequently withdrawn from these bank accounts by the scammers.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: The modus operandi of these malware-related scams has been extensively covered in an earlier joint advisory from the Police, Government Technology Agency (GovTech) and CPF Board on 29 June 2023.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: In gist, the victims downloaded malware-infected Android Package Kits, or APK, from unauthorised sites and they subsequently turned on accessibility services when told by the scammer to purportedly facilitate the purchase of items at a steep discount.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Doing so allowed the scammer to take full control of the phone, steal banking and Singpass credentials stored in the phone and perform unauthorised CPF log-ins and withdrawals.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We should update our phones regularly with the latest security patches and we should only download apps from official app stores and exercise the greatest of caution when we are prompted to turn on accessibility services.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: These accessibility services are mainly meant to assist users with disabilities to use their devices, such as by allowing apps to read and control your screen.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Members may be asked to perform Singpass Face Verification (SFV) or other checks when accessing CPF e-services.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: This provides additional security in addition to the existing two-factor Singpass authentication required for accessing CPF e-services.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Members who require assistance on CPF services and the SFV can visit the CPF service centres and Singpass counters respectively.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: These additional safeguards may make it slightly less convenient for members to perform certain CPF e-services but I think members would agree that it is better to be safe than sorry.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: This is especially so in light of new threats.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: The Government will continue to review and monitor these threats closely and work closely alongside the banks to introduce more precautionary measures where necessary.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: The Police will spare no effort in tracking down those responsible for such malware incidents and will take tough action against them.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: I urge anyone with information on such crimes to contact the Police immediately.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: I am heartened that the Government has placed this additional precaution to require CPF members who log in to their accounts using their Singpass to go through face verification.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: I believe this will go some way in patching one of the vulnerabilities inherent in the Android platform that allows scammers to install malware on the users' phone.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: My constituency, Radin Mas, has a large proportion of seniors aged 60 and above.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: So, while we actively encourage our seniors to embrace digitisation, I am also well aware that they will also become vulnerable to such scams.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: So, what is the Ministry's estimate or projection on the proportion of such malware scams that can be prevented or thwarted with the implementation of such face verification?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: I think the Minister earlier mentioned a ninth case was successfully prevented by the Police.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: So, how is the Ministry of Manpower (MOM) or CPF Board working with SPF to better detect and prevent unauthorised transfers of CPF monies?

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: For the demographics of the victims – the victims are between the ages of 55 and 80.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: From the CPF safeguards, there are the additional precautionary measures that we have now undertaken, even though we constantly monitor many of these scams because they get very creative.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Thus far, we think that it is sufficient to effectively limit the convenience in terms of the withdrawal of monies from the CPF accounts to their own bank accounts.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I understand that the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) – with GovTech, the banks and also SPF – are separately working on a parallel initiative to see how to protect banking customers from allowing unauthorised withdrawals from their bank accounts.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: From the CPF Board's perspective, the additional steps that we have put in as a precautionary measure, allowing the member to separately require Singpass Face Verification, is an added step.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: And some members would inevitably say that that has resulted in a lot more inconvenience for them to withdraw their amount.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: But we think that this is actually necessary to protect their hard-earned monies.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: For the separate track, that would probably require a separate Parliamentary Question with regard to the banking relationships with the account holders; how the steps have been effective in limiting withdrawal or unauthorised withdrawal from these banking accounts.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: I am wondering if the Minister can share a little bit about whether the Government has also considered initiatives along the lines of insurance.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: I mention this, in part, because as I am sure his is aware, in usual banking related frauds, insurance plays a big part in helping to recover fraudulent monies and in this case, CPF is both mandatory savings scheme but is also a very, very big supplier.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: So, it may be possible to secure a fairly competitive insurance rate for the purposes of doing this kind of additional protection.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Indeed, we are considering that part of it.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: This is under the Shared Responsibility Framework, which involves the financial institutions, the telcos and many other participating entities.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: So, I suggest that perhaps, at that particular point in time, we can delve deeper into the details.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Is MOM working with GovTech to patch this vulnerability if it, indeed, is about the vulnerability?

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Perhaps, Mr Giam may not have an appreciation of the different steps that these scammers sort of would navigate to actually get the CPF members to download these apps.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Today, the vulnerability appears to be in the Android phones and generally our members may have just gone online, whether it is on Facebook or some other form of social media, and come across some particular app which purportedly gives him a steep discount; a very, very good deal, in which they have to download that particular app.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: And once they download the app, they will, more often than not, get phone calls from someone helping them to navigate and to use the app.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: And they then hand over some of the navigational options to this and turn on the accessibility services on their Android phone itself.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We have these identities stored, because the NRICs, the passports, we have that.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Based on our records, we can then ensure that the person who is logging in and making these withdrawals actually corresponds to the actual member and not through some scam account.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: So, we believe that, today, that added step, which to some members cause a lot of inconvenience, is sufficient as a precautionary measure.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: To clarify, I understand the process in which the scammers use to access the phone.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: But just now the Minister said that once the accessibility is enabled, the scammers are able to read the passwords that are stored in Singpass.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: Typically, these passwords should not be stored at all inside the phone.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: So, I just want to understand whether or not this is something that is being looked into, as to why is it that passwords are stored inside the phone for that reason?

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I think there are a myriad of reasons why people store their passwords on the phones, in their notepads and so on.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: There are also members who write it down somewhere in a booklet and they put it at home.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Of course, I said that there are also parallel initiatives to deal with what happens after the money goes into the banking account.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: So, there are all these measures that we are doing.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I would not want to be in a position of hubris where we say that we have got it all figured out.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: So, we have to constantly work at nudging our people, working with one another to keep reminding all of our members, all of our citizens to always be vigilant.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: I raised my hand, but I think Minister Tan had already made the point.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The information is being taken from other parts of the phone, not as Mr Giam had asked about.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: But the point has been made by Dr Tan already.
